description: An analysis tool for Python that blurs the line between testing and type systems.

summary.one_liner: CrossHair is a Python analysis tool that checks type-annotated functions and contracts by running them on symbolic inputs solved with an SMT solver, blurring the line between testing and type systems.
summary.what_it_does: CrossHair repeatedly calls your Python functions with symbolic inputs and uses an SMT solver to explore viable execution paths and look for counterexamples. If a function has type annotations and a contract in a supported syntax, it tries to find inputs that violate the contract. It claims symbolic reasoning across built-in types, user-defined classes, and much of the standard library. Beyond contract checking, the README says it can generate unit tests and find behavioral differences between functions (the "diffbehavior" command). The README also mentions a browser version at crosshair-web.org and IDE integrations for VS Code and PyCharm, and notes that Hypothesis can use CrossHair as an optional backend.
use_cases: find counterexamples for type-annotated Python functions
compare behavior of two Python functions
try static-style checking in the browser
notable: Symbolic execution of Python with an SMT solver, covering built-in types, user classes, and much of the standard library
Can generate unit tests and find behavioral differences between functions
Optional backend for the Hypothesis property-based testing tool
IDE integrations for VS Code and PyCharm, plus a browser demo
caveats: README does not include install or run commands in the provided text; see the Get Started docs
Works on contracts in a supported syntax only; coverage of Python features is listed under Limitations in the docs, not detailed here
